content.comment_body: Hello everyone, regarding this topic, I am having an issue where my Aq remains at 0 in simulation mode. I notice input values do change, but Aq does not respond. Any advice would be appreciated.

Your screenshot quality is poor, so I cannot accurately see your programming details. It appears you are using a mathematical instruction where the enable input (EN) is connected to a HIGH block, but you are also negating EN. This is equivalent to using a LOW block instead of HIGH with no negation. To resolve this, choose one option: either connect to a HIGH block and do not negate EN, or negate EN.

[Forum Related] @ixo65: Could you clarify what problem you see with the image? I personally do not notice a rendering issue, though the forum makes it appear small, so zooming in (Ctrl + mouse scroll) helps. Alternatively, opening and saving the image in another browser tab improves visibility. I have attached the image with no edits. Were my notes useful? Or does "bad quality" refer to something else?
Hello [user_name], remove the inversion at block B003 or disconnect your connection to that block. Greetings, [user_name] (translated via Google)

analysis.insight_summary: Users are struggling to understand why analog output (Aq) stays at 0 during simulation even with changing inputs. The confusion comes from applying both a HIGH signal and its negation to the enable input (EN) of a mathematical instruction, causing the block to be disabled. This points to a need for clearer guidance on enabling logic within the software interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect Aq output to react directly to input changes in simulation mode, without needing complex troubleshooting of logical blocks.
